newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks steady at open, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks steady at open, slow trade.

text.p: The Australian share market was steady at the opening on Friday with some modest but positive interest in resource leaders ensuring the market held the line.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index edged up 0.4 points to 2,247.5. The September share price index lost one point to 2246, a 1.5 point discount to the underlying index.

With slight turnover and a choppy, albeit narrow trading range seen so far, brokers said a typical Friday showing looked likely with only BHP's first quarter results to generate much interest. BHP is due to report before 0200 GMT.
"There is some selective buying in resources stocks BHP, CRA and MIM off a low base, but there is not much outside of those," said Derek Bond, director at brokerage Burrell and Co.
Bond singled out National Australia Bank among the indutrials, but noted the overall market focus remained on BHP.
"National Australia Bank is enjoying its recent publicity and pushing towards the A$13.00 mark but really all attention is on BHP awaiting the result," he said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to four, while 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
